In Fig. 2[1], panel C gives the mean genome GC content of S. marcescens as μ = 59.74%[2]. A dashed line marks the mean on the histogram, and most genomes sit near the peak at about 60.0%[3].

Panel D plots coding GC against intergenic GC. They have a positive correlation of r = 0.57[4], which is statistically significant (p < 0.001[5]). The fitted line slopes upward, so coding GC rises as intergenic GC rises.

These values were read from the figure image. OCR also confirms the mean, but the correlation values were read only by the vision model.[6][7]

source.caption: Fig. 2. Phenotypic characteristics and genomic diversity of S. marcescens. (A) Temperature-dependent prodigiosin pigmentation phenotype; (B) distribution of the prodigiosin biosynthetic gene cluster among different biogroups; (C–D) GC content and genomic compositional characteristics; (E) pangenome composition and genomic variability; and (F) predicted host range of plasmids identified in S. marcescens. The figure summarizes the multi-level diversity of S. marcescens in phenotype, genome composition, and genetic plasticity.
